locations.name: An all-night record shop stacked to the ceiling
The base of the TV tower, glowing red
A 24-hour döner counter three blocks from the venue
A stretch of the old wall, repainted a hundred times

collaborator.gift: a patch cable, still coiled the way she left it

preShowChoices.label: Cut the click track entirely
preShowChoices.description: Play it loose. Let the room set the tempo tonight.

preShowChoices.label: Push the PA to the edge
preShowChoices.description: Loud enough to feel it in your teeth.

preShowChoices.label: Trade the bridge with Lene's modular rig
preShowChoices.description: Hand four bars to a machine that's never played it the same way twice.

minigames.title: Modular Check
minigames.introText: Jun's rig is four boxes deep and none of them are labelled. "Just play back what you hear," she says, entirely unhelpfully.
minigames.outroText: Four patterns, no notes written down. Jun looks personally vindicated by the whole exercise.
minigames.outroTextRough: You lose the thread halfway through and Jun patches around it, unbothered, already onto the next idea.

minigames.title: Synth Soundcheck
minigames.introText: Lene's already patched half the rig. "Give me a level before the room fills up."
minigames.outroText: "Clean," Lene says, already reaching for another cable. "Same time tomorrow?"
minigames.outroTextRough: "A little hot," Lene shrugs, "but that's kind of the whole point of a modular rig."

ber_arrival.speaker: narrator
ber_arrival.text: The van dies in traffic under the TV tower's red blinking eye, and somehow nobody's mad about it — Berlin doesn't seem to care if you're late, it just keeps going without you either way.

choices.label: Watch the light hit the tower
Get the gear off before the meter runs
Check on Theo, who's gone unusually quiet

ber_arrival_view.speaker: narrator
ber_arrival_view.text: The tower blinks red, steady, indifferent to all of you. Somewhere below it, a hundred clubs are only just now opening their doors for the night.

ber_arrival_gear.speaker: narrator
ber_arrival_gear.text: The parking attendant doesn't even glance up from his phone. Everyone in this city, it seems, has somewhere else they'd rather be right now.

ber_arrival_theo.speaker: theo
ber_arrival_theo.text: "This city doesn't sleep, and apparently neither will I," Theo says, staring up at the tower like it personally owes him an explanation.

ber_loc_powerplant.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_powerplant.text: Turbines the size of buses, rusted into accidental sculpture. Someone from tonight's other act is already running cable across the concrete floor, whistling something you almost recognize.

choices.label: Watch the other band's soundcheck
Offer to help carry cases

ber_loc_powerplant_watch.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_powerplant_watch.text: Their bassist nods at you once, like a password quietly exchanged between strangers who understand exactly what the other one is carrying.

ber_loc_powerplant_watch_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_powerplant_watch_after.text: You never speak to them. You never need to. Two bands, one night, the same nerves in different clothes.

ber_loc_powerplant_help.speaker: jun
ber_loc_powerplant_help.text: "This whole place used to run half the city," Jun says, hauling a case, grinning like it's somehow Christmas morning.

ber_loc_powerplant_help_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_powerplant_help_after.text: The cases are heavier than they look. Jun carries three anyway, talking the entire time about turbines.

ber_loc_records.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_records.text: Krautrock reissues stacked against techno white labels stacked against a whole shelf in a language none of you can read. The owner doesn't look up from his paperback.

choices.label: Dig for something you can't identify
Ask the owner for a recommendation

ber_loc_records_dig.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_records_dig.text: No label, no year, no country listed anywhere on the sleeve. You buy it purely on the strength of the cover art alone.

ber_loc_records_dig_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_records_dig_after.text: It plays as badly as it looks. Track four is the best thing you have heard in a month.

ber_loc_records_ask.speaker: mira
ber_loc_records_ask.text: "He just handed me something with no cover at all," Mira says, delighted, already turning the blank sleeve over in her hands.

ber_loc_records_ask_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_records_ask_after.text: She won't let anyone else touch it until she has heard it through once, alone, with the door shut.

ber_loc_biergarten.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_biergarten.text: Fairy lights strung between murals of faces nobody remembers the names of anymore. Somebody's dog is peacefully asleep under every third table in the courtyard.

choices.label: Toast to nothing in particular
Find the quietest corner and just breathe

ber_loc_biergarten_toast.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_biergarten_toast.text: Glasses clink around the table. Nobody actually asks what for. That's apparently just how it's done here, no explanation required.

ber_loc_biergarten_toast_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_biergarten_toast_after.text: The table beside yours toasts too, for reasons of their own. You never find out what. It does not matter.

ber_loc_biergarten_quiet.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_biergarten_quiet.text: For twenty whole minutes, the only job in the world is existing quietly in a plastic chair. You turn out to be surprisingly good at it.

ber_loc_biergarten_quiet_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_biergarten_quiet_after.text: Theo falls asleep sitting upright. Nobody wakes him. The chair holds. The evening holds.

ber_loc_tower.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_tower.text: The base of the tower hums faintly — some machinery deep inside still working after all these decades. From down here, the whole city looks like a lit, patient circuit board.

choices.label: See how far up the stairs go before they're locked
Rowan's already sitting against the base, not talking

ber_loc_tower_climb.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_tower_climb.text: Four flights up, a locked gate stops you cold. The view from that landing is still, somehow, entirely worth the climb.

ber_loc_tower_climb_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_tower_climb_after.text: Coming down takes longer than going up. It always does, and you always forget that going up.

ber_loc_tower_rowan.speaker: rowan
ber_loc_tower_rowan.text: "I like it better from down here," Rowan says. "Less obvious that you're the one being looked at, for once."

ber_loc_tower_rowan_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_tower_rowan_after.text: You sit down beside them. The tower keeps blinking. Neither of you says anything else for a while.

ber_loc_doner.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_doner.text: Three in the morning and the line is still eight people deep, mostly folks who look like they haven't yet decided whether the night is actually over.

choices.label: Order the thing everyone else is ordering
People-watch instead of ordering anything

ber_loc_doner_order.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_doner_order.text: It's exactly as good as the line outside promised it would be. Worth every minute of the wait, barely.

ber_loc_doner_order_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_doner_order_after.text: You eat standing up, in the cold, at one in the morning. It goes straight into the permanent record.

ber_loc_doner_people.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_doner_people.text: Nobody in this line looks like they're actually from anywhere in particular. Somehow, for once, you fit right in.

ber_loc_doner_people_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_doner_people_after.text: Four people from four places, in a line at a counter, none of them explaining themselves to anyone.

ber_loc_wall.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_wall.text: A stretch of the old wall, repainted so many times the newest layer is already flaking to show three others underneath. Nothing here is meant to last — that seems to be the entire point.

choices.label: Leave something small of your own
Try to read the layers underneath

ber_loc_wall_add.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_wall_add.text: A single stray line, gone within the week probably, painted over by someone who'll never know it was yours to begin with. Somehow that feels exactly right.

ber_loc_wall_add_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_wall_add_after.text: You photograph it badly, on purpose, so the memory has to do most of the work later.

ber_loc_wall_read.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_wall_read.text: A date from decades ago, half a name, a phone number that surely doesn't ring anymore. History here doesn't get preserved so much as simply outlived.

ber_loc_wall_read_after.speaker: narrator
ber_loc_wall_read_after.text: Mira reads one out loud. Nobody laughs. It wasn't funny, and it wasn't meant to be.

ber_rel_mira.speaker: mira
ber_rel_mira.text: "Nobody here has any idea who we are," Mira says, watching the crowd. "Which should feel like freedom, and mostly just feels like nothing at all."

choices.label: That's exactly what makes it freedom
Let her sit with the nothing a while

ber_rel_mira_a.speaker: mira
ber_rel_mira_a.text: She doesn't fully buy the reframe. But she stops arguing with it, which turns out to be its own quiet kind of yes.

ber_rel_mira_b.speaker: mira
ber_rel_mira_b.text: "Okay," she says eventually, to the tower, not really to you at all.

ber_rel_theo.speaker: theo
ber_rel_theo.text: "I haven't slept right since Lisbon," Theo admits. "This whole city runs on no sleep at all. I genuinely don't know if that helps me or ruins me."

choices.label: Find him somewhere actually quiet to crash
Match his hours instead of fighting them

ber_rel_theo_a.speaker: theo
ber_rel_theo_a.text: He's asleep within nine minutes flat. You count, somehow, though you couldn't say exactly why that matters to you.

ber_rel_theo_b.speaker: theo
ber_rel_theo_b.text: By dawn you've written half a new song together and completely forgotten what day of the week it even is.

ber_rel_jun.speaker: jun
ber_rel_jun.text: "What if we ran the whole set through something that's broken on purpose," Jun says, already holding a cable that clearly, visibly shouldn't work at all.

choices.label: Let's actually try it tonight
Save it — we can't risk tonight

ber_rel_jun_a.speaker: jun
ber_rel_jun_a.text: "Tonight then," Jun says, already halfway to the stage before you've even finished agreeing to it.

ber_rel_jun_b.speaker: jun
ber_rel_jun_b.text: Jun shrugs, entirely unbothered, and starts sketching the idea out for some later, safer night instead.

ber_rel_jun2.speaker: jun
ber_rel_jun2.text: "Found someone who builds her own synths out of spare parts," Jun says, practically vibrating. "She said I could sit in on tonight's set, if we're brave enough to let her." Not budgeted for. Landing hard anyway.

choices.label: Say yes before you can talk yourself out of it
Ask what "brave" actually means here first

ber_rel_jun2_a.speaker: jun
ber_rel_jun2_a.text: "Brave," Jun repeats, delighted, already typing out a reply before you've fully finished saying yes — already replaying how tonight's going to sound before it's happened.

ber_rel_jun2_b.speaker: jun
ber_rel_jun2_b.text: "Fair question. Honestly, I don't fully know either," Jun admits. "That might be sort of the whole point."

ber_rel_rowan.speaker: rowan
ber_rel_rowan.text: "Everyone here already has a scene," Rowan says, watching the crowd. "We're just passing through it." It doesn't sound like a complaint. It sounds closer to grief.

choices.label: You're building your own, one city at a time
Maybe that's just what touring actually is

ber_rel_rowan_a.speaker: rowan
ber_rel_rowan_a.text: Rowan doesn't answer out loud, but the bass case opens a little more easily than it did an hour ago.

ber_rel_rowan_b.speaker: rowan
ber_rel_rowan_b.text: "Yeah," Rowan says quietly, mostly to the pavement. "Maybe that's just what this whole thing actually is."

ber_rel_mira2.speaker: mira
ber_rel_mira2.text: A street musician outside the venue waves off a passerby's cash — busking for the sound, not the coins, apparently. "I used to think wanting anything back made it fake," Mira says. "Now I'm not so sure."

choices.label: Maybe wanting it doesn't make it less real
Go ask her what she actually thinks

ber_rel_mira2_a.speaker: mira
ber_rel_mira2_a.text: "Yeah," she says slowly, like she's trying the sentence on for size. "Yeah, maybe both things are just true at once."

ber_rel_mira2_b.speaker: mira
ber_rel_mira2_b.text: The busker just laughs. "Ask me after rent's due," she says, and keeps playing anyway, unbothered either way.

ber_rel_rowan2.speaker: rowan
ber_rel_rowan2.text: Three strangers with a borrowed drum machine wave Rowan over mid-jam in the alley behind the venue — nobody asks a name, nobody cares about the tour. Just: can you keep this groove going.

choices.label: Jump in without a second thought
Watch a round before joining

ber_rel_rowan2_a.speaker: rowan
ber_rel_rowan2_a.text: Nobody claps when the groove locks in. Nobody needs to. Rowan grins the whole walk back, not saying why.

ber_rel_rowan2_b.speaker: rowan
ber_rel_rowan2_b.text: By the second round Rowan's in, uninvited-but-welcome, and nobody in that alley ever does learn a single name.

ber_preshow.speaker: narrator
ber_preshow.text: The power-plant venue fills fast — all denim and boots and nobody once checking their phone. Tonight's shape, like every night's, is still entirely yours to choose.

ber_aftershow.speaker: narrator
ber_aftershow.text: The crowd doesn't so much leave as dissolve into whatever's happening next somewhere else in the city — a party, another set, a sunrise nobody planned on staying up for.

choices.label: Follow the crowd to whatever's next
Head straight back to the bus instead

ber_aftershow_record.speaker: narrator
ber_aftershow_record.text: Someone backstage has a turntable, of course they do. You play the unlabeled record once, start to finish, and still can't tell what country or decade it's actually from.

choices.label: Follow the crowd to whatever's next
Head straight back to the bus instead

ber_aftershow_a.speaker: narrator
ber_aftershow_a.text: You don't remember most of what happened after. You do remember, clearly, not wanting any of it to end.

ber_aftershow_b.speaker: narrator
ber_aftershow_b.text: The bus is quiet and still. Somewhere outside, the whole city keeps going without you, same as always.

ber_journal.speaker: narrator
ber_journal.text: You write: Lene's rig never plays the same thing twice, and somehow the soundcheck was the cleanest read all week. Berlin never once cared whether we were there. We stayed anyway, and it let us. Onward.

ber_journal_generic.speaker: narrator
ber_journal_generic.text: You write: Berlin never once cared whether we were there. We stayed anyway, and it let us. Onward.
